description:
Surfaced 2026-04-27 by the
`verify-ci-validation-workflow-end-to-end` end-to-end test (PRs #27,
#28, #29 against `published-results`).

The two halves of the Phase 2 submission flow disagree on what
"bundle" the manifest hash covers:

- `benchbox/cli/commands/submit.py:_compute_bundle_hash` hashes
  `output_path/bundle/` — the isolated package directory containing
  only the new submission's files. Manifest written with this hash.
- `scripts/validate_submission.py:_validate_manifest_hash` hashes
  `bundle_path.parent`, where `bundle_path` is the changed bundle
  file under `results-data/bundles/`. That parent already contains
  every other bundle in the corpus.

So the submitter hashes one file; the validator hashes ~13. They
can never match.

Evidence: even an unmodified `benchbox submit --last` package fails
the validator with a hash mismatch on PR. See
`_project/handoffs/ci-validation-evidence-2026-04-27.md`.

**Impact**: every Phase 2 community PR submission fails CI today
regardless of content. Phase 2 is not actually shippable in its
current form.

anti_patterns.dont: 'fix' this by hashing the entire results-data/bundles/ directory in the submitter
anti_patterns.why: that requires the submitter to clone the full corpus and stay synced

anti_patterns.dont: bury the contract in a code comment
anti_patterns.instead: write it down in an ADR or in scripts/validate_submission.py's docstring.
anti_patterns.why: the next agent will repeat the same divergence

preserves.behavior: Existing schema-v2 bundle format. The fix is a contract change in the manifest, not the bundle.
Phase 2 PR-based submission flow remains the only supported submit path until Phase 3 stands up.
Validator continues to reject obvious tampering (the hash-mismatch and schema-invalid cases captured 2026-04-27 must still fail post-fix).

verifications.description: Re-run E2E test against published-results: happy path is green
verifications.expected: PASSED status on a new test PR

work_units.notes:
Two paths:

A. **Per-file hash** (recommended): the manifest's `bundle_hash`
   is the SHA-256 of the bundle's primary JSON file (and
   optional companions, as separate fields). The validator
   recomputes per-file and compares. This matches the
   architecture-design doc's content-addressed storage scheme
   (each bundle is a single content hash regardless of corpus
   co-location).

B. **Directory hash** (status quo on validator side): the
   manifest's `bundle_hash` is over a directory, but the
   submitter must compute that hash with the *same set of files*
   as the validator. This forces the submitter to know the
   corpus state — a bad coupling.

Pick A. Document the decision in an ADR fragment under
`docs/development/adr/` if it warrants one (probably yes — this
is a contract change).
work_units.summary: Decide which side defines the contract: per-file hash or directory hash

work_units.notes:
Update `benchbox/cli/commands/submit.py:_compute_bundle_hash`
and `scripts/validate_submission.py:_validate_manifest_hash` so
they compute the same value for the same logical input.

For path A (recommended), the manifest gains a per-file hash
map:

    {
      "bundle_hash":  "<sha256 of primary bundle file>",
      "companion_hashes": {
        "<filename>.plans.json":  "<sha256>",
        "<filename>.tuning.json": "<sha256>"
      }
    }

Validator iterates the map; mismatches cite the offending file
and the offending hash side (manifest vs computed).
work_units.summary: Update both implementations to match the chosen contract

work_units.notes:
A round-trip test: package via the submit command, copy bundle
+ manifest into a fixture mimicking results-data/bundles/ with
*other* bundles already present, run the validator. Must pass.

A hand-corrupt test: same flow but flip a byte; validator must
fail with a clear message.

Both tests live under `tests/integration/test_submission_validation.py`.
work_units.summary: Add unit tests covering the contract on both sides

work_units.notes:
Open one new test PR against `published-results` with a
maintainer-run small bundle. Confirm: workflow accepts on the
happy path, the corpus-inventory check runs and either passes or
gives a clear "out of date" message, the PR-comment is updated
idempotently after a no-op recommit. Append the new evidence to
`_project/handoffs/ci-validation-evidence-*.md`.
